title: Microsoft 365 Fundamentals
subtitle: Jeopardy Review

jeopardyFormatExample.clueText: This M365 cloud email service gives Business-plan users a 50 GB mailbox.

categoryLegend: Six MS-900 domains: cloud concepts, M365 apps, teamwork, identity & security, compliance, and licensing & support.

clues.clue: Microsoft 365 falls into this cloud service model, where the provider manages everything from infrastructure to the application itself.
clues.response: What is SaaS (Software as a Service)?
clues.explain: In SaaS, the vendor delivers a fully managed application over the internet. Microsoft hosts and maintains M365; users simply log in and use it without managing any underlying infrastructure.

clues.clue: This cloud deployment model uses only one provider's infrastructure, dedicated solely to a single organization and not shared with other tenants.
clues.explain: A private cloud is hosted exclusively for one organization, offering greater control and isolation. Public clouds share infrastructure across many customers; hybrid clouds combine both models.

clues.clue: Switching from buying physical servers (CapEx) to paying a monthly subscription for cloud services is a shift to this type of spending model.
clues.explain: CapEx involves large upfront capital purchases, such as buying servers. OpEx means paying for resources as you consume them, which is the model cloud subscriptions like M365 use.

clues.clue: Under the shared responsibility model in M365, Microsoft is responsible for securing physical datacenters and network infrastructure, while the customer remains responsible for this.
clues.response: What is identity, data, access, and devices?
clues.explain: Microsoft secures the underlying infrastructure in SaaS, but customers must manage who has access (identity), what data they protect, and the security posture of devices connecting to the service.

clues.clue: The Microsoft Online Services SLA guarantees at least this percentage of uptime for Microsoft 365 core services, forming the contractual basis for service credits if targets are missed.
clues.explain: The 99.9% uptime SLA means no more than about 8.7 hours of downtime per year per service. If Microsoft falls below this threshold, customers can request service credits under the SLA terms.

clues.clue: This Microsoft 365 cloud storage service for individuals gives each user 1 TB of default storage and syncs files across their devices.
clues.explain: OneDrive for Business provides each licensed user 1 TB of personal cloud storage. It syncs files to desktops and supports Files On-Demand, which downloads a file only when it is opened.

clues.clue: This OneDrive for Business feature automatically redirects a user's Desktop, Documents, and Pictures folders to the cloud without requiring them to manually move files.
clues.explain: Known Folder Move (KFM) silently redirects the three key Windows folders to OneDrive for Business, ensuring those files are backed up and available on any device.

clues.clue: Microsoft 365 Apps licenses allow each user to install the full Office desktop suite on up to this many PCs or Macs, plus 5 tablets and 5 phones.
clues.explain: Each Microsoft 365 Apps license permits installation on up to 5 PCs/Macs, 5 tablets, and 5 phones per user, with a concurrent active-session limit of 5 devices at any one time.

clues.clue: Exchange Online mailboxes on E3 and E5 plans include this much storage per user - double the capacity provided on Business plans.
clues.explain: Business plans (Basic, Standard, Premium) include 50 GB Exchange Online mailboxes. Stepping up to E3 or E5 doubles that to 100 GB per user, plus both include auto-expanding archiving.

clues.clue: When two co-authors edit the same Word document stored in OneDrive or SharePoint at the same time, this feature immediately saves their changes without requiring them to click Save.
clues.explain: AutoSave activates automatically when a file is stored in OneDrive for Business or SharePoint Online. Combined with co-authoring, it lets multiple users edit simultaneously while version history preserves every prior state.

clues.clue: This Microsoft 365 hub for teamwork brings together chat, video meetings, file sharing, and app integrations into a single interface.
clues.explain: Microsoft Teams is the primary collaboration hub in M365. It integrates persistent chat, channel-based conversations, video conferencing, and file collaboration all in one place.

clues.clue: Files shared inside a Microsoft Teams channel are stored in this Microsoft 365 service, not inside Teams itself.
clues.explain: Every Teams channel is backed by a SharePoint Online document library. Files posted in a channel are actually stored in that library, which is why users can access them via SharePoint even outside Teams.

clues.clue: Microsoft Teams video meetings support up to this many participants, making it suitable for large all-hands events and town halls.
clues.explain: Standard Teams meetings support up to 1,000 participants. For larger events, Teams Town Halls (formerly live events) can scale significantly higher, but the standard meeting cap is 1,000.

clues.clue: This Microsoft 365 service, formerly known as Yammer, provides company-wide social networking and community discussion across an organization.
clues.explain: Viva Engage is the rebranded Yammer, now part of the Microsoft Viva employee experience platform. It enables organization-wide communities, open discussions, and leadership communications beyond team-level chat.

clues.clue: When a user sends a private 1:1 or group chat message in Microsoft Teams, those messages are actually stored in this underlying Microsoft 365 service.
clues.explain: Teams private chat messages are stored in a hidden Exchange Online mailbox folder for each user, making them searchable via eDiscovery and subject to retention policies configured in Microsoft Purview.

clues.clue: This Microsoft cloud identity service, formerly called Azure Active Directory, is the foundation for sign-in and access control across Microsoft 365.
clues.explain: Microsoft Entra ID (renamed from Azure AD in 2023) is the identity backbone of M365. It handles authentication, SSO, group management, and integrates with thousands of SaaS applications.

clues.clue: Enabling this security feature is credited with blocking approximately 99.9% of account-compromise attacks by requiring a second proof of identity beyond a password.
clues.explain: MFA requires users to verify their identity through a second method such as an authenticator app or phone call. Microsoft's data shows MFA alone prevents roughly 99.9% of automated credential attacks.

clues.clue: This Microsoft Defender component acts as a Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB), giving admins visibility into shadow IT and unsanctioned cloud app usage.
clues.response: What is Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps?
clues.explain: Defender for Cloud Apps is M365's CASB solution. It discovers unsanctioned SaaS apps in use across the organization (shadow IT), assesses their risk, and can enforce policies to block or limit access.

clues.clue: This Entra ID feature uses if/then logic - evaluating signals like user location, device compliance, and sign-in risk - to grant, block, or require step-up authentication for access. It requires at least Entra ID P1.
clues.explain: Conditional Access policies evaluate contextual signals at sign-in time and apply a matching access decision. For example: if a user signs in from an unmanaged device in a risky location, require MFA or block access. Requires Entra ID P1.

clues.clue: The Zero Trust security model is built on three core principles: verify explicitly, use least privilege, and this third principle that assumes an attacker may already be inside the network.
clues.explain: The three Zero Trust principles are: verify explicitly (always authenticate and authorize using all available signals), use least privilege (limit access with JIT/PIM), and assume breach (minimize blast radius by segmenting and monitoring as if a breach has already occurred).

clues.clue: These Microsoft Purview labels classify and protect documents by applying encryption and usage restrictions, and they travel with the file wherever it goes.
clues.explain: Sensitivity labels in Microsoft Purview attach metadata and optional encryption or watermarks directly to a file. Because the protection travels with the document, it remains enforced even if the file is emailed outside the organization.

clues.clue: This Microsoft Purview policy type automatically detects and prevents users from sharing sensitive information such as credit card numbers or Social Security numbers across Exchange, SharePoint, Teams, and endpoints.
clues.explain: DLP policies in Purview scan content in real time for sensitive data patterns. When a match is found - such as a credit card number in an email - the policy can block the action, notify the user, or generate an alert for administrators.

clues.clue: This Microsoft Purview tool gives organizations a score reflecting how well they meet regulatory compliance requirements, and provides recommended improvement actions.
clues.explain: Compliance Manager assesses an organization's posture against frameworks such as GDPR, HIPAA, and ISO 27001. It calculates a compliance score and surfaces specific actions admins can take to close gaps.

clues.clue: Data at rest inside Microsoft 365 services is encrypted using this Microsoft technology that operates at the volume level on Windows servers in Microsoft datacenters.
clues.explain: Microsoft uses BitLocker full-volume encryption to protect data at rest on datacenter servers. Data in transit is protected with TLS 1.2 or higher. Both layers are part of Microsoft's encryption commitments under the shared responsibility model.

clues.clue: An auditor needs to download the actual SOC 2 Type II report for Microsoft 365. They should go here - an authenticated portal - rather than the public Trust Center website.
clues.response: What is the Service Trust Portal (servicetrust.microsoft.com)?
clues.explain: The public Trust Center (microsoft.com/trust-center) describes Microsoft's broad privacy and security commitments. The Service Trust Portal requires authentication and provides downloadable third-party audit reports such as SOC, ISO, and FedRAMP documentation for customer review.

clues.clue: Microsoft 365 Business plans - Basic, Standard, and Premium - are capped at this maximum number of users per tenant.
clues.explain: All three Microsoft 365 Business plans have a 300-seat ceiling. Organizations needing more than 300 licensed users must move to Enterprise plans (E1, E3, or E5), which have no user cap.

clues.clue: This Microsoft 365 Business plan is the only one among the three Business tiers that includes Microsoft Intune for device management plus advanced security features.
clues.explain: Business Basic and Standard lack Intune and advanced security. Business Premium bundles Intune, Entra ID P1, Defender for Business, Azure Information Protection P1, and Microsoft Purview - making it the security-focused Business tier.

clues.clue: This is the only Microsoft 365 Enterprise plan that includes Defender for Endpoint Plan 2, Teams Phone System, and Power BI Pro as built-in components.
clues.explain: E3 includes desktop apps, Intune, and Entra ID P1 but not advanced Defender, Phone System, or Power BI Pro. E5 is the top-tier plan that adds Entra ID P2, Defender suite P2, Teams Phone System, and Power BI Pro.

clues.clue: This free Microsoft program provides remote deployment guidance for organizations with 150 or more eligible Microsoft 365 licenses, helping them onboard services at no extra cost.
clues.explain: FastTrack offers remote-only deployment assistance from Microsoft engineers at no charge for tenants with 150 or more eligible licenses. It covers onboarding for core M365 workloads but does not include on-site support or customization work.

clues.clue: An admin needs to know when Microsoft plans to retire a feature in the Microsoft 365 admin center. This specific admin center section delivers advance notices of upcoming changes, with Microsoft committing to at least 12 months warning under Modern Lifecycle.
clues.explain: The Message Center in admin.microsoft.com posts advance notices of new features, changes, and retirements. Under the Modern Lifecycle Policy, Microsoft provides a minimum 12-month deprecation notice so admins can plan transitions. Service Health, by contrast, reports current incidents and outages.
